scope: Grouped completed data, source/CPU, training, collection, blind-review submission, reference-amendment, amended adjudication, seal verification and scoring evidence. checks.scope: Detailed independent model review provenance, every family decision and fault, exact rematerialization, retained semantic preservation and final executable gate.
limitations: Semantic reviews are model-authored, not human gold. Passing admission establishes review coverage and state consistency, not improved tracking quality.

checks.scope: Exhaustive lexical comparison of 19,700 cross-split pairs, triaged semantic screening and post-replacement review of changed training families.
limitations: Only the explicitly identified important pairs received full-dialogue review; screening is model-based and cannot prove absence of leakage. Cross-language similarities may be missed. Five-decision authoring templates and short histories remain shared.

checks.scope: Six fault types, repair replay, causal source arrival, target history preservation/removal, deduplication and paired confidence-interval direction.
limitations: The position-ledger review is a historical pre-semantic-revision snapshot; final data admission and the final 240-fault invariant check cover the admitted inputs. CPU fixtures do not establish model output quality.

checks.scope: Frozen training mathematics, 600 unique three-arm assignments and six balanced orders, prompt label exclusion, adapter-state fixtures, durable attempt recovery and exclusive process lock.
limitations: The last receipt binds an earlier gate/compiler/evaluator revision; its trainer and collector bindings remain the frozen versions. Later final data-gate, repair-logic and workflow receipts cover their revised components. Actual runtime adapter state and completed collection remain separate checks.

checks.scope: Synthetic 600-assignment workflow, candidate deduplication, secondary-review selection, manual judgment validation, sealing and frozen-evaluator integration.
limitations: Synthetic fixture judgments do not count as real blind review or a real seal. Filesystem checks cannot prove reviewer independence. Production review must retain initial judgments, adjudication and seal verification evidence.

checks.scope: Endpoint definitions and signs, 40-family paired bootstrap, joint decision rule, explicit comparison conditions and protocol lock before training.
limitations: Single seed, synthetic model-reviewed data and one-step supplied-state testing limit inference. No own-state rollout, natural-user or independent long-dialogue generalization is established. Protocol acceptance is not a positive experiment outcome.

checks.scope: Actual final-data tokenizer inspection, total training length and completion-only supervision without truncation.
limitations: This is tokenizer/data validation, not model inference. Real collection prompt lengths must still be reconciled to reviewed per-row test lengths and frozen summary.

checks.scope: Actual completed formal-01 run: terminal exit evidence, full event sequence, unique row order, frozen recipe, finite numerical values, final partial update, adapter-only save and one-probe reload.
limitations: Training completion, finite loss and reload equality do not establish reduced intention omissions.
The final partial-group divisor is verified in executed source; phase logs contain no divisor or gradient tensors.
Save/reload equality and enabled/disabled difference cover one training-input last-position logit probe only.

Base freezing relies on audited source/assertions and LoRA-only saved matrices. Cached base payloads were size-checked against the previously verified receipt, not rehashed or compared before/after this run.
The audit reads saved logs/artifacts and neither inspects live GPU tensors nor reruns training or tokenization.

checks.scope: Training-log mutation fixtures and hand-computed result/cost/paired-CI fixtures for the independent auditors.
limitations: The training auditor was subsequently applied to the completed run in its own check above. The result auditor has only synthetic fixtures so far; no real numerical or narrative result audit has been completed.

checks.scope: Fail-closed evidence gates, attempt and cost accounting, source stability, privacy projection and unchanged split export checks.
limitations: These checks use synthetic fixtures or existing support files. Actual completed outputs, sealed judgments, reviewed interpretation and final numerical audit must pass before any real export.

checks.scope: Static source/schema and metric-label review, interval directions, denominator consistency, historical-bundle preservation contract and public evidence wording.
limitations: This is static review only. Actual data build, preservation rehash, numerical/display reconciliation, browser QA and publication remain pending. The common builder is not transactional; final output requires verification after a build.

checks.scope: Actual completed single-epoch training tokens and host elapsed training time; no quality or efficiency attribution.
limitations: The same 500 examples and 32 optimizer updates do not match actual token count or FLOPs.
Training time is one observed run per adapter, not a controlled hardware performance benchmark.

checks.scope: Root terminal/completeness check plus frozen evaluator replay and dispatch. This does not certify semantic accuracy; final independent numerical audit is still pending.
limitations: Successful generation does not imply a valid patch or a correct state update.
Runtime validity is a structural result, not semantic quality.
At the original preparation stage, reviewer attestations, second reviews, adjudication and final sealed scoring were still required; later completion is recorded separately.
Physical attempt accounting cannot prove the absence of unrecorded calls.

checks.scope: Frozen gate rejected invalid review accounting and reference-flag encoding; original reviewers corrected their own submissions under blindness and preserved original bytes.
limitations: Successful preparation verifies coverage, provenance and schema; it does not establish semantic correctness.
Reference-scope and evidence disputes were then submitted to the independent blinded adjudicator; the resulting reference-defect block and amendment are recorded separately.
Reviewer checks initially missed these structural conflicts; original submissions and failed gate receipts are preserved.

checks.scope: Synthetic amendment/carry-forward fixtures and independent amendment-aware recount/export source review. These checks precede actual result review and do not validate semantic outcomes.
limitations: The 36-check helper and 32-check export suites use synthetic data; their checks are not additional semantic reviews or experimental model calls.

The original helpers, evaluator, review workflow, protocol and compiled splits remain unchanged. Named identities and attestations do not cryptographically establish independent reasoning.

checks.scope: Post-collection, pre-aggregation repair of two incomplete reference texts under the frozen protocol. Original artifacts remain available, and only a new expected-reference preparation is used for subsequent scoring.
limitations: Two explicit preservation qualifiers had been omitted from the supplied reference states despite prior data admission. The independent fresh semantic approval covered the two selected complete arrived dialogues and all their reference entries; it was not a new full-test semantic audit.

The correction was copied to every model variant for each affected input. Reference identities, owners, statuses, counts, raw inputs, model outputs, candidate operations, runtime records and prospective second-review selection remained fixed.

The reference ledger reasons include candidate-specific observations from their original seed. Reviewers were explicitly instructed to inspect each candidate itself; conditions retained by another candidate must not be treated as omitted. Public reason_scope discloses this distinction.

The same original six review contexts rechecked seven affected assignments and carried forward 837 unchanged judgment records byte-for-byte. Completion verification is structural provenance plus reviewer attestation, not proof of semantic correctness.
Original primary and secondary accounting corrections and the two failed preparation attempts remain documented in the preceding group.
The later amended adjudication, sealing and scoring completion is recorded in the following group; independent numerical and narrative result audit remains downstream.

checks.scope: Actual amendment-specific review-completion gate, amended adjudicator carry-forward, sealed-review structural replay and frozen-evaluator scoring. No independent numerical or narrative approval is asserted here.
limitations: The 40 required amended adjudications reused the same independent adjudicator's original resolved decisions only after equality checks on all 40 packets and 76 included initial judgments. This was zero fresh semantic adjudicator rereviews, not 40 new independent judgments.

The two original defective cases no longer required adjudication after reference correction and affected initial re-review. Their original unresolved decisions and findings remain preserved; the adjudicator did not independently reread every uncontested amended packet.

The same six initial reviewers supplied explicit same-context re-review/carry-forward attestations. Structural verification and named attestations do not prove honest context isolation or semantic correctness.

Sealing and successful scoring establish completed execution over model-authored judgments, not human gold or a positive research result. Actual metrics and narrative require the separate fresh independent final audit.
Only a one-step supplied-state experiment was scored. These checks do not test own-state rollout, chat/work delivery, natural user assistance, ASR, user studies or dynamic role routing.
